Sharing behavior
Private by default
Read receipts and typing indicators are under your control.

On: paired devices skip the per-capability prompt and get full access. Off: you approve each new pairing's reach. Trust costs nothing until it does.

Encrypts your local database at rest. Set the ONE_LINK_PASSPHRASE environment variable before launching One Link. It's a 2014 vibe, but it works.

Read receipts

On: peers see ✓✓ once you've actually read their message. Off: peers never learn what you've read. They'll cope.

Off: your sent messages stay at ✓ no matter what. Useful if "Read" lives rent-free in your head.

Typing indicators

On: peers see the little dots while you compose. Off: peers wonder. We think wondering is a feature.

Off: the typing banner never appears, no matter how furiously someone is typing at you.

Blocked devices

Blocked devices can't pair, send, or vibe in your direction. Unblock here if you've forgiven them.

Nobody on the list. Yet.

Notifications

Browser-level system notifications. Per-device mute (in the device drawer) wins over this. A muted peer never pings, no matter how loudly they yell.

What to notify about

Include message text in the desktop notification. Off if your lock screen is read by people you didn't invite.

Pings when a peer adds or removes an emoji on something you said. Off if you don't need to know who 👍'd what.

Sound
Do-not-disturb

During quiet hours, notifications and chimes shut up. Messages still arrive; they just don't make a scene. Crosses midnight (e.g. 22:00 → 07:00).

Appearance

Control the whole feel of One Link: palette, density, message shape, motion, and chat background.

Accent color

Applies immediately to buttons, focus rings, unread accents, and the outgoing message gradient.

Light mode flips the palette for the unhinged among us. "Match system" tracks your OS preference live.

Chats

Make conversation behavior explicit: sending, scrolling, previews, receipts, typing, and pairing defaults.

Devices yelling on your local network are paired without asking. Off: you approve each one manually, like a person who reads EULAs.

Per-conversation settings (disappearing messages, mute, custom alias) live on the gear next to each device or group in the sidebar.

Storage & data

Downloads

Files land here. Leave blank for the built-in inbox. Pick a folder that already exists and is writable.

Default disappearing messages

Applies to NEW devices you pair from here on. Existing chats keep whatever TTL is on their device drawer; we don't time-travel into old conversations.

Bandwidth limit

Caps One Link's combined send + receive throughput. Useful on a metered connection, or if you'd like the rest of the internet to keep working.

Auto-accept files

Inbound files that pass these rules land in your inbox quietly. Anything outside (too big, or extension not in the allowlist) gets bounced. Sorry, we have standards (you set them).

Clear app traces

These actions erase One Link's local records only. They do not delete files or folders from your computer, and they do not revoke your identity or paired devices.

The wipe clears chats, file-transfer records, folder metadata, activity/audit rows, route memory, and local UI trace settings. Actual files stay where they are.

iPhone first time? (one-time trust setup)

iOS won't let Safari bypass a self-signed cert warning on a LAN address. To fix this once per phone, install the trust profile below. After install you can scan the regular pair QR with no warnings ever again on this phone.

  1. Scan the trust-profile QR below, or copy the URL.
  2. When iOS asks to download a configuration profile, tap Allow.
  3. Open Settings - General - VPN & Device Management, then install One Link Trust.
  4. Open Settings - General - About - Certificate Trust Settings, then trust One Link Root CA.
  5. Scan the pair QR above.

Advanced

Operator controls for diagnostics, runtime support bundles, deep health checks, and truth-status inspection.

Log verbosity

Affects One Link's terminal log + the diagnostics overlay. "Debug" surfaces every wire frame and CRDT merge. Useful when something is misbehaving; noisy otherwise.

Troubleshooting

Live error log + a health check. Open this only if something feels off. In normal use you'll never need it, which is the dream.

Share a diagnostic snapshot

Build a redacted report (your version, OS info, paired-peer count, recent error log) you can save or paste into a bug report. Identifying info (display name, peer fingerprints, message bodies) is stripped first.

One Link Doctor

Quick health check across every surface that has to work for messages, files, and calls. Tells you what's healthy, what's degraded, and what to do.

One Link is peer-to-peer LAN chat + file sync. End-to-end encrypted by default. No account, no server, no telemetry. Your data stays on your devices. We barely even know what files are.

Built on Coherence; yes, we drank our own kool-aid. Source on GitHub

A key change is benign when the device was reinstalled or replaced - but if you didn't expect one, treat it as a potential impersonation. Re-pair only after confirming the new identity through a side channel.

Disappearing messages

When set, every new TEXT message to (or from) this device gets a self-destruct timer. Both sides see the same countdown; rows tombstone automatically when due. Files and reactions don't expire. Only chat text.

Chat wallpaper

Folder sync conflicts

Two devices changed the same file at the same time. Pick which version wins for each file. Choosing "Keep both" preserves your version under its original name AND saves the other device's version with a .conflict-<peer> suffix so nothing is lost.

No conflicts. Everyone agrees, for once. ✓

Reach devices across the internet?

Right now One Link only finds devices on the same Wi-Fi network. That's perfect for household use - nothing else to set up.

To reach devices in other locations (a laptop at home from a coffee shop, family across town), you need a tiny relay called a rendezvous. It only carries signed presence beacons - never your messages or files.

How to set one up (advanced)
  • Use a rendezvous a friend or community is running - paste their URL into Settings → Rendezvous URLs.
  • Run your own - free, ~5 minutes, see RENDEZVOUS_DEPLOY.md in the repo.
